symbols.name: chirp position
symbols.meaning: An integer position at which the chirp is evaluated, which may be negative or at least $q$.
symbols.quote: Let $\sigma$ be an integer position, which may be negative or at least $q$.

symbols.name: scaled input
symbols.meaning: The vector $u$ with each coordinate divided by its chirp entry.

symbols.name: cyclic convolution
symbols.meaning: The cyclic convolution of two length-$q$ sequences, with indices taken modulo $q$.
symbols.quote: For length-$q$ sequences, $a\ast b$ denotes the cyclic convolution with $(a\ast b)_\ell=\sum_{s=0}^{q-1}a_s\,b_{(\ell-s)\bmod q}$.

symbols.name: coordinatewise product
symbols.meaning: The product of two vectors taken entry by entry.
symbols.quote: Writing $a\cdot b$ for the coordinatewise product, $(a\cdot b)_s=a_sb_s$, this is $\hat u=\frac1\chi\cdot u$.

relations.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_q$ of even length $q$ as a convolution multiplied by chirp factors.
It reduces the transform to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), so any method that computes that convolution also computes the transform.
The identity is applied inside the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), which keeps the permutations in the formula.

In the argument it turns the [middle transform](middle-transform.md), including its target permutation, into a [normalized cyclic convolution](normalized-cyclic-convolution.md), which the paper's convolution method can compute.
The identity gives its cost with the [logarithm](logarithm.md) $\lg q$, the exponent to which $2$ must be raised to give $q$: if the convolution costs $O(q\lg q)$ steps, so does the transform.
For even $q$ the wrap-around carries no sign, so the identity avoids a [negacyclic convolution](negacyclic-convolution.md), a convolution in which a wrap-around picks up a minus sign.
